account: The node's dossier includes the full text of the Smit et al. file (papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt), so the required evidence is present in the workspace. However, the parent node's acceptance condition requires three distinct categories of findings: (1) MAD not reliably outperforming other prompting strategies, (2) performance comparisons on specific benchmarks, and (3) limitations or sensitivity to hyperparameters. These are distinct evidence questions that can be answered independently by separate child nodes, each collecting anchored quotes or close paraphrases with exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers. Splitting them into parallel extraction tasks reduces the risk of missing a category and allows each child to focus on a separate facet of the null result. The parent can then synthesize the three sets of findings into the required three-plus findings. Given the remaining depth is 1 and node budget is 7, expansion with three children is feasible and parallelizable. Therefore, expand is chosen.

children.acceptance_condition: Returns at least one finding consisting of a direct quote or close paraphrase from the Smit file, with the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where it appears, explicitly stating that MAD does not reliably outperform other prompting strategies such as self-consistency or ensembling.
children.expected_contribution: A source-anchored finding that MAD lacks reliable superiority over single-agent or ensemble prompting baselines, with page markers.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: All required text is contained in the enclosed Smit file; no sibling output is needed to select, quote, or paraphrase the finding.
children.objective: Extract from papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt at least one anchored finding stating that multi-agent debate (MAD) does not reliably outperform other prompting strategies (e.g., self-consistency, ensembling), quoting or closely paraphrasing the relevant passage(s) and carrying the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s).
children.rationale: This is the first and most important null result: the paper's abstract and conclusions emphasize that MAD, in its current form, does not reliably outperform other prompting strategies. This finding is distinct from specific benchmark numbers and hyperparameter sensitivity, and it grounds the reconciliation requirement (D11) and the quality metric family (D14).
separator_facts: The evidentiary corpus is exactly seven extracted-text files under papers/text, including smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt.
Page boundaries in the extracted texts are marked with lines of the form `===== PDF PAGE N =====`.
Citations must carry the exact page markers (D12).

children.acceptance_condition: Returns at least one finding consisting of a direct quote or close paraphrase from the Smit file, with the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), that reports performance numbers or rankings on at least two named benchmarks comparing at least one MAD system against a non-debate baseline.
children.expected_contribution: A source-anchored finding with benchmark-specific numbers or rankings, showing MAD does not consistently beat baselines, with page markers.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: The relevant text is inside the enclosed Smit file; no sibling data is needed to extract the benchmark comparisons.
children.objective: Extract from papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt at least one anchored finding that compares performance of MAD systems against single-agent or other prompting baselines on specific benchmarks (e.g., MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, CosmosQA, CIAR, GPQA, Chess), quoting or closely paraphrasing the relevant table or sentence and carrying the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s).
children.rationale: The acceptance condition requires coverage of performance comparisons on specific benchmarks. The paper includes Table 2 and Figure 3 comparing best performance across seven datasets, and states 'no protocol dominates on all datasets'. Capturing this provides quantitative grounding for the evaluation plan's quality and matched-compute considerations (D14).
separator_facts: The Smit file contains Table 2 with best performance scores on MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, CosmosQA, CIAR, GPQA, and Chess.
Page boundaries are marked with `===== PDF PAGE N =====`.

children.acceptance_condition: Returns at least one finding consisting of a direct quote or close paraphrase from the Smit file, with the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s), that states either a limitation of the study or that MAD performance is sensitive to hyperparameters (e.g., agreement intensity) and thus difficult to optimize.
children.expected_contribution: A source-anchored finding on hyperparameter sensitivity or study limitations, with page markers, for D15 and evaluation-plan constraints.
children.no_future_sibling_dependency: All required text is within the enclosed Smit file; the child does not need any sibling's output to extract the limitation or sensitivity statement.
children.objective: Extract from papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt at least one anchored finding stating limitations of the study or sensitivity of MAD to hyperparameters (e.g., agreement intensity, number of agents/rounds), quoting or closely paraphrasing the relevant passage(s) and carrying the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s).
children.rationale: The acceptance condition requires coverage of stated limitations or sensitivity to hyperparameters. The paper's abstract and Section 4 explicitly state that MAD protocols are more sensitive to hyperparameter settings and difficult to optimize, and the limitations paragraph in the conclusions mentions API variability and cost. This finding grounds D15 (limitations) and informs the evaluation plan's hyperparameter control.
separator_facts: The Smit file's abstract and conclusions discuss hyperparameter sensitivity and difficulty of optimization.
Page markers `===== PDF PAGE N =====` delimit pages.

decidability.account: The full text of the Smit file is enclosed in the dossier, providing the grounded referent for all extraction. The acceptance condition is not fully mechanical because it requires selecting quotes or close paraphrases that are relevant to three thematic categories and carrying their exact page markers; this requires judgment in selection and paraphrase. The node is independent of future siblings because it relies only on the enclosed Smit file, with no dependency on outputs from any other child.

synthesis_contract.acceptance_condition: The synthesized answer includes at least three distinct findings, each with page markers, covering all three required thematic areas, and each finding is traceable to a specific page marker.
synthesis_contract.conflict_policy: If any child returns a finding that contradicts another (e.g., a benchmark number that seems to favor a MAD system), the parent will still include it and explicitly reconcile it by noting the paper's overall summary that no protocol dominates. Conflicting evidence is preserved, not hidden (C4).
synthesis_contract.parent_question: Extract at least three anchored findings from Smit et al. covering (1) MAD not reliably outperforming other prompting strategies, (2) performance comparisons on specific benchmarks, and (3) stated limitations or sensitivity to hyperparameters.
required_contributions: child smit-extract-null-overall: one anchored finding that MAD does not reliably outperform other prompting strategies (e.g., self-consistency, ensembling).
child smit-extract-benchmarks: one anchored finding with benchmark-specific comparisons showing MAD not dominating on at least two datasets.
child smit-extract-limitations-hyperparams: one anchored finding on hyperparameter sensitivity or study limitations.
shared_invariants: All findings must be direct quotes or close paraphrases from the Smit file.
Each finding must carry the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where the quoted or paraphrased passage appears.
No outside sources may be used (C2).
